items.summary: Gradio introduces gr.Workflow, a tool that allows users to create AI pipelines as graphs of nodes. key_points: NVIDIA's Vera CPU is designed to balance single-thread performance and concurrency for agentic AI workloads.
Telemetry from 163,594 sessions shows agentic tasks have highly variable trajectories with long sequential chains and sporadic parallel bursts.
Traditional CPU designs struggle to accommodate this variability, either sacrificing latency or failing to handle parallel demands.
The Vera CPU's Olympus cores maintain strong per-thread performance while providing sufficient concurrency for parallel workloads.
NVIDIA claims the Vera CPU delivers up to 1.5x agentic performance compared to competitors, improving fleet economics.
items.summary: NVIDIA's Vera CPU is designed to address the challenges of agentic AI workloads by balancing single-thread performance and concurrency. Based on telemetry from 163,594 sessions, agentic tasks exhibit highly variable trajectories with long sequential chains and sporadic parallel bursts. Traditional CPU designs struggle to accommodate this variability, as they either prioritize core count at the expense of latency or fail to handle transient fan-out demands. The Vera CPU, with its Olympus cores, maintains strong per-thread performance while providing sufficient concurrency to manage parallel workloads. This design reduces latency on the critical sequential path and absorbs intermittent bursts of parallel computation. NVIDIA claims the Vera CPU delivers up to 1.5x agentic performance compared to competitors, improving fleet economics by maximizing completed user sessions. The architecture also minimizes memory and power overhead, ensuring efficient resource utilization across the entire workload trajectory.
items.title: NVIDIA Vera CPU Optimizes Agentic AI Workloads with Balanced Performance

items.summary: NVIDIA has introduced Cosmos 3 Edge, a 4B omni-model designed for real-time on-device robot control. The model, part of the Cosmos 3 family, is pretrained on physical-world data and optimized to run on NVIDIA Jetson Thor, addressing memory and latency constraints for robotic applications. items.summary: Professor Dimitri Bertsekas, a renowned computer scientist and prolific author, died at 83. key_points: IBM Research proposes an abstraction layer for cryptography to simplify security operations and reduce technical debt.
Current cryptographic practices embed algorithm choices in application code, leading to fragile systems and operational complexity.
The proposed intent-based API separates cryptographic policy from implementation, allowing centralized management of security decisions.
The initiative includes a partial reference implementation and an API specification, inviting community testing and refinement.
The approach is positioned as a necessary evolution for handling post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and future cryptographic changes without code modifications.
items.summary: IBM Research introduces a new approach to cryptographic agility by proposing an abstraction layer that separates cryptographic decisions from application code. Developers currently manage complex security operations manually, embedding algorithm choices directly into code, which leads to fragile systems and technical debt. The proposed solution, inspired by filesystems and networking abstractions, aims to centralize cryptographic policy and allow runtime enforcement of security decisions. The initiative includes an intent-based API that defines cryptographic scopes, enabling interchangeable algorithms within defined categories. This shift would transform cryptography from a development concern to an operational one, managed by security teams. IBM has released an API specification and a partial reference implementation, inviting the community to test and refine the approach. The work is framed as a necessary evolution in response to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) adoption, which requires significant system rearchitecture. The goal is to create a sustainable framework that reduces developer burden and enables future cryptographic changes without code modifications.
items.title: IBM Research proposes cryptographic abstraction layer to simplify security operations

key_points: Google introduces Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) to retrofit existing Gemini Nano v3 models for improved on-device AI efficiency.

The technique enables faster AI features like notification summaries and text proofreading without compromising model accuracy.

items.summary: Google researchers introduce a method to retrofit Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) onto existing Gemini Nano v3 models, improving on-device inference efficiency. This approach addresses the limitations of autoregressive text generation on mobile devices, which are constrained by energy and memory limits. By integrating a lightweight MTP head into the model's final layers, Google reduces memory usage and processing time, enabling faster AI features like notification summaries and text proofreading. The MTP head leverages the main model's internal state to predict future tokens, eliminating the need for separate, memory-heavy drafters. This retrofitting technique maintains the original model's accuracy and safety while achieving up to 50% speed improvements on Pixel 9 devices. Google also highlights further optimizations, including parallel decoding and verification leniency, to enhance performance under mobile constraints.
items.title: Google Enhances On-Device AI Efficiency with Multi-Token Prediction on Pixel Phones

items.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has expanded its mass spectral library, known as Standard Reference Database 1A, to include hundreds of thousands of chemical fingerprints. The library contains 382,180 entries in the Electron Ionization (EI) component and 68,635 in the Tandem Library. NIST scientists use a software-based evaluation process to ensure accuracy. The updated database is available for purchase and is preinstalled on many commercial mass spectrometers.
items.title: NIST Updates Chemical Fingerprint Library to Identify Unknown Substances

key_points: Apostol Vassilev's proof shows no finite guardrails can fully protect AI from adversarial prompts.
The research builds on Gödel's incompleteness theorems, demonstrating inherent limitations in formal systems.
Attackers can bypass AI guardrails through carefully crafted prompts, leading to real-world risks.
Vassilev suggests a continuous security model with red teams, updates, and resilience to counter evolving threats.
The goal is to make the cost of exploiting AI systems exceed attackers' resources, creating a new economic equilibrium.
items.summary: Apostol Vassilev, a senior scientist at NIST, published a mathematical proof in IEEE Security and Privacy, demonstrating that no finite set of guardrails can fully protect AI systems from adversarial prompts. The proof builds on Kurt Gödel's 1931 incompleteness theorems, which showed limitations in formal systems. Vassilev explained that while guardrails can prevent AI from generating harmful content, attackers can craft prompts to bypass these rules, effectively 'jailbreaking' the system. The research highlights that adversarial prompts will always exist, but the complexity of language makes finding and exploiting vulnerabilities extremely difficult. Vassilev proposed a continuous security model involving red teams, regular updates, and operational resilience to stay ahead of attackers, aiming to make the cost of exploitation exceed attackers' resources.
items.title: NIST Proof Shows AI Guardrails Can't Fully Prevent Adversarial Attacks

items.summary: Amazon's Project Eluna, an agentic AI model for fulfillment centers, relies on four approaches to ensure physical consistency and operational reliability. These methods include physics-guided deep learning, which integrates physical laws into model training; uncertainty-aware reasoning, which calibrates confidence in predictions; bridging the text-to-numerical gap through adaptive learning and simulation tools; and verifier-augmented grounding, which uses external checks to validate outputs. The article highlights how these techniques address challenges like hallucination and ensure safe, reliable AI operation in complex physical environments. The approaches aim to enable AI agents to function effectively in domains such as logistics, healthcare, and climate science, with the potential for broader application as the technology matures.
items.title: Amazon's Project Eluna Uses Four Approaches to Ground AI Agents in Physical Reality

items.summary: Mistral introduces physics AI as a foundational tool to accelerate engineering processes across industries. Researchers emphasize that cancer is not a single disease, and personalized approaches may be necessary for different tumor types. Other trials are underway for lung, bladder, and kidney cancers, with experts highlighting the need for more affordable alternatives like oncolytic viruses.
items.title: Personalized cancer vaccines show promise in melanoma treatment

items.summary: India's sugar market has shifted from a projected surplus to a severe shortage, causing prices to rise sharply. Initially, the government and industry expected a 18.3% increase in sugar production to 34.90 million tonnes for the 2025-26 season, leading to early export approvals. However, production estimates were repeatedly revised downward due to factors like crop damage, weather issues, and lower-than-expected ethanol diversion. By May, the government banned sugar exports to preserve domestic supplies, and prices surged to record highs, reaching ₹7,100 per 100kg in some regions. The government responded by tightening stockholding limits and opening sugar imports. Analysts criticized the reliance on industry forecasts, noting that ISMA's initial estimates were consistently optimistic. The ethanol policy also played a role, as lower-than-expected diversion to ethanol reduced sugar availability. With closing stocks projected to fall to near two-decade lows, concerns remain about the next season's production, especially with El Niño conditions threatening sugarcane yields in key states.

items.summary: Google Cloud researchers propose linear elastic caching, a method that dynamically adjusts cache size to minimize costs while maintaining performance. Traditional fixed-size caching leads to either underutilized memory or poor performance, but linear elastic caching treats memory as a variable cost. items.summary: Massachusetts lawmakers are cautioning against proposed fixed charges in energy bills that could disproportionately increase electricity costs for low-use customers. The bills, passed by both the House and Senate, aim to lower energy costs through measures like flexible interconnection and solar permitting. However, fixed charges—shifted from volumetric charges—could raise bills for at least 60% of ratepayers, particularly affecting low-income households and small businesses. SEIA's analysis shows the bottom 25% of residential users would see bills rise by over 10%, while top users would save money. items.summary: Global land-use emissions, including deforestation and forest degradation, have fallen by 32% since the 2000s, according to the 2025 Global Carbon Budget report. items.summary: Margaret Olley, a celebrated Australian painter, graduated from the National Art School in 1945 with first-class honours. items.summary: Three MS-13 members testified under a cooperation agreement with Salvadoran prosecutors that between 2013 and 2021, they buried over 200 victims at Finca Suiza, a wooded area in Nuevo Cuscatlán where former president Nayib Bukele began his political career. items.summary: Indian benchmark stock indices Sensex and Nifty opened lower on Tuesday, August 25, amid escalating US-Iran sanctions and falling crude oil prices. Key Sensex firms like Adani Ports and Axis Bank underperformed, while Tata Steel and HCL Tech were among the top gainers. Brent crude prices fell 1.68% to $92.80 per barrel.

items.summary: Ahmad Faraz, a prominent Urdu poet, is celebrated for his ability to blend classical discipline with contemporary precision in his ghazals. His work, marked by a unique balance of intellectual rigor and emotional depth, has left a lasting impact on both performance and written poetry. Faraz's verses, such as 'Ranjish hi sahī' and 'Ab ke ham bichhre', are noted for their intricate structure and philosophical insights, often addressing themes of desire, ethics, and political commitment. His poetic style, characterized by strategic use of rhyme and rhythm, made his work accessible yet profound, resonating with both critics and general audiences. Faraz's commitment to social and political issues is evident in his magnum opus 'Muhāsarā', where he asserts the poet's responsibility to the people rather than to power. His legacy endures through the continued relevance of his work in both literary and musical contexts.

The government terminated the contract in 2024, and the firm sold for Rs 1 crore, highlighting broader issues in India's waste management sector.

items.summary: A Chinese waste-to-energy firm, Ecogreen Energy Pvt Ltd, invested Rs 428 crore in its Indian operations in Gurugram and Faridabad, with the government adding Rs 157 crore. Despite promises to reduce the Bandhwari landfill, the site grew to 38 metres high, polluting groundwater. Company records show funds were diverted to related firms, consultancy fees, and unfulfilled machinery purchases. In 2024, the government terminated the contract, and the firm sold for Rs 1 crore. The failure reflects broader issues in India's waste management, with multiple companies failing to deliver on public contracts. Ecogreen's contracts, including a 22-year Rs 330-crore agreement, were awarded despite its dormant status. The company outsourced waste collection to local scrap dealers, bypassing contractual obligations. The National Green Tribunal fined the government Rs 100 crore for environmental damage, highlighting the cost of failed public spending.

key_points: Assam farmers are integrating rice and crab farming to adapt to climate change and erratic weather patterns.
Indigenous rice varieties like Betguti, which can withstand long dry spells, are being cultivated alongside freshwater crabs that improve soil health and reduce pest problems.
Supported by the Assam State Rural Livelihood Mission, this women-led initiative is expanding across 219 blocks, with farmers reporting increased income and reduced agrochemical use.
Research indicates that rice-crab farming enhances soil fertility, biodiversity, and productivity while promoting sustainable agricultural practices.
Women farmers like Nikumoni Bora have achieved financial success, earning over ₹1.35 lakh through rice and crab harvests, and are encouraging others to adopt the method.
items.summary: Farmers in Assam are adopting an integrated rice-crab farming method to address climate challenges. Women cultivate indigenous rice varieties like Betguti, which can withstand erratic weather, and raise freshwater crabs that help control pests and aerate soil. Supported by the Assam State Rural Livelihood Mission, this approach is being scaled across 219 blocks. The crabs provide an additional income source and reduce reliance on agrochemicals. Research highlights benefits such as improved soil fertility and biodiversity. Women like Nikumoni Bora have seen success, earning over ₹1.35 lakh through rice and crab harvests. The initiative aims to promote indigenous rice varieties and enhance nutritional security through community-led farming efforts.
items.title: Assam farmers integrate rice and crab farming to combat climate change

key_points: Glaciers in the Zanskar Himalayas have slowed by 16% in velocity from 1992 to 2023, with lower elevation glaciers losing speed faster.
Accelerated ice thinning accompanies the slowdown, threatening water security for Ladakh, which relies on glacier melt.
Scientists link the changes to global warming, which is reducing precipitation in the region and affecting glacier health.
The study, using satellite data, highlights the need for better predictions of glacier behavior to manage water resources in the Indus river basin.
Glacier retreat across the Himalayas, including the HKH region, has led to a 12% area loss between 1990 and 2020.
items.summary: A new study shows glaciers in the Zanskar Himalayas of Ladakh have slowed by 16% in velocity from 1992 to 2023, with lower elevation glaciers losing speed faster. This slowdown, linked to accelerated ice thinning, threatens water security for the region, which relies on glacier melt. Scientists note that glacier velocity reflects their health, as mass accumulation at higher elevations drives movement. The study, published in The Cryosphere, used satellite data to track changes, finding that glacier thinning accelerated from 0.22 to 0.57 meters per year between 2000-2005 and 2015-2020. Researchers attribute the changes to global warming, which is reducing precipitation in the area. The findings add to growing concerns about glacier retreat across the Himalayas, with the HKH region experiencing a 12% area loss between 1990 and 2020.
items.title: Ladakh glaciers slow down as ice melts, threatening water supply
